key_insight: ChronoSyn uses the chronology of materials discovery as an additional learning signal to improve predictions of which hypothetical compositions are experimentally realizable.
engineering_relevance: The model could help prioritize synthesis candidates from large computational and generative materials libraries.
method: Learn a shared representation of material composition.
Jointly predict synthesizability and the relative reporting order of known materials.
Score hypothetical compositions to identify promising chemical families.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved prediction over baseline models and screening of approximately 50 million hypothetical compositions, with high-scoring families containing experimentally reported compositions unseen during training.
watch_item: Reporting chronology may reflect research priorities and historical biases as well as synthesis feasibility; prospective experimental validation is not described in the abstract.
paper_title: Learning the Chronology of Materials Discovery for Synthesizability Prediction
